suggestions.quote: She went to sleep in Leipzig with East German marks and woke up with Deutsche Marks (c04). Her savings above a line, cut in half (c04).
suggestions.fix: In 1990, she went to sleep in Leipzig with East German marks and woke up with Deutsche Marks, her savings above a line cut in half (c04).

suggestions.quote: One once credited a customer eighty-one trillion dollars by mistake, and reversed it within hours (c07).
suggestions.fix: One once credited a customer 81 trillion dollars by mistake, and reversed it within hours (c07).

suggestions.quote: Mansa Musa once came through Cairo and gave away so much gold that gold there stayed cheap for at least twelve years (c06).
suggestions.fix: In 1324, Mansa Musa came through Cairo and gave away so much gold that gold there stayed cheap for at least twelve years (c06).

keep.quote: Her grandfather's story. The king and the chessboard (c05). A grain doubles on every square. By the end, the board owes more wheat than the whole world grows in over a thousand years (c11).
Berlin once ran this race the other way. By late 1923, a loaf there cost about two hundred billion marks (c01). Many workers spent their wages the moment they were paid (c02).

Day fifty-five. The number passes what the whole world makes in a year. Every loaf, every car, every hour of work on Earth. About 128 trillion dollars (c09). You have more than that. In euros. Above a bakery. And tomorrow is twice this.
